answer: Reputation-anchored identity decay. Each agent identity carries a reputation score tied to a signed action log, and only agents whose score exceeds a threshold can issue new identities; issuance consumes a raven-marked credit that decays over time, so unused credits expire. Cloning an identity resets its score to zero, forcing the attacker to rebuild history from scratch, while a forged relic of prior actions is rejected by cross-signed checkpoints. The concrete cost is the time and compute to earn each credit plus the walnut-sized reputation proof stored per clone,
